articles.title: Barcelona vs Real Madrid: La Liga – El Clasico preview, predictions, teams
articles.excerpt:
Who: Barcelona vs Real Madrid
What: La Liga, El Clasico
Where: Camp Nou in Barcelona, Spain
When: Sunday at 9pm (20:00 GMT)
How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up and live upd...
articles.body_text:
Who: Barcelona vs Real Madrid
What: La Liga, El Clasico
Where: Camp Nou in Barcelona, Spain
When: Sunday at 9pm (20:00 GMT)
How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up and live updates from 17:00 GMT.

For weeks La Liga leaders Barcelona have been eagerly awaiting Sunday’s El Clasico as a chance to stretch the gap between themselves and rivals Real Madrid to a massive nine points.

Some turbulence in the final approach to the clash at Camp Nou has complicated the picture for Hansi Flick’s Spanish champions, who suffered their first defeat of the season at Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Tuesday.

By contrast, Real Madrid have won four consecutive matches, thrashing RB Leipzig on Wednesday and starting to look, for the first time since Jose Mourinho’s arrival this summer, like a team.

Should Real come away with a win, it would not only halve the current six-point gap, but ⁠provide a much-needed confidence boost for a side that has lost six of the last seven Clasicos.

Mourinho’s return to the fixture will attract the most attention of all.

The ⁠63-year-old is a veteran of 27 matches against Barcelona and 17 El Clasicos on ⁠the Real bench.

Real Madrid President Florentino Perez first appointed Mourinho as manager in 2010 to compete with Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona, and he will hope the Portuguese can wrest the La Liga title back to the Bernabeu for a second time.

Mourinho’s first spell at Real coincided with arguably the most heated encounters in ‌the modern history of El Clasico, and there will be numerous cameras trained on his every move at Camp Nou on Sunday.

The Portuguese manager won just once in his first 10 El Clasicos but went unbeaten in his final five games ‌against ‌Barcelona, recording three victories.

Flick’s Barca have won back-to-back La Liga titles and lead the top flight, in which they are unbeaten, while Mourinho arrived this summer after Madrid went two seasons without a major trophy.

Mourinho highlighted that he has been at the helm only a few months in comparison with Flick, who arrived at Barca in 2024.

“People look at us like a finished product, but finished products in football are difficult because they are never finished, … but they look at us like we’re in an advanced phase of the process,” Mourinho continued.

“We’ve been working for three months. Out of that you can take preseason when the players were arriving [back from the World Cup] and the recent international break. Then we’ve been together a month-and-a-half, two months.

“This is the start of a product. We’re in an initial phase where the coach is learning, analysing, bit by bit defining paths. The players are learning about the coach. … Comparing a team in this state [to more established sides], I think is unfair.”

The German coach said he expected a Madrid side arriving with “a lot of confidence” and praised Mourinho.

“I have the highest respect. When you’re managing teams on this level for so many years and you always have success, it’s about quality. He showed this at every club,” Flick told reporters.

“Every player from the [German] national team who worked under him speaks with a great respect. I think the same. He’s a colleague, a very, very successful colleague and a great colleague.”

Flick said the 4-2 defeat in Paris by PSG on Tuesday gave his team some clues as to where they need to improve.

“We analysed this game. We did many things really good, but we saw some situations where we have to improve,” Flick said.

“We have to grow as a team. Tomorrow we play against one of the best teams in the world, so it’s a good opportunity to grow, to challenge ourselves, to improve ourselves and to grow as a team.”

Flick: “El Clasico is different. It is the best match in our sport, and everyone will watch it. It is incredible. It is true that we are playing for just three points, but the importance of the match goes far beyond that.”

Mourinho: “We’ve been in a good dynamic, winning games, playing well, scoring goals, but in El Clasico, it doesn’t matter what you did before. It has no influence. El Clasico is unique. Normally, the football world stops to watch it. Hopefully, it’s a great game and we win.”

Barcelona have a perfect record in La Liga with nine wins from nine games. They are five points clear at the top of the standings.

Their only defeat in all competitions this season came in the last match, in which they fell 4-2 to title holders PSG in the Champions League league phase.

Real are third in the La Liga points table, six points behind leaders and rivals Barca.

They have won seven league games but lost to Atletico Madrid and Real Betis.

However, Real have made a perfect start in the UCL, registering two wins in as many matches.

Opta’s supercomputer has given Barcelona a 54.4 percent chance of winning this Clasico while Real have a 26.1 percent probability. There are 19.5 percent odds of a draw.

Overall, Barca are given a 77.93 percent chance of retaining the title this season with Real tipped to finish second and Atletico third.

Midfielder Dani Olmo will miss the Clasico after being ruled out for about a month with a thigh injury.

Other names already on the injury list are Jules Kounde (ankle), Eric Garcia (thigh), Andreas Christensen (thigh) and Roony Bardghji (knee).

Joan Garcia (goalkeeper); Xavi Espart, Pau Cubarsi, Gerard Martin, Joao Cancelo; Marc Bernal, Pedri; Lamine Yamal, Ferran Torres, Anthony Gordon; Raphinha

Vincius Jr will miss the game due to a suspension while Raul Asencio (leg) and Rodrygo (knee) are both injured.

Thibaut Courtois (goalkeeper); Federico Valverde, Antonio Rudiger, Dean Huijsen, Alvaro Carreras; Bernardo Silva, Eduardo Camavinga; Arda Guler, Jude Bellingham, Yan Diomande, Kylian Mbappe

articles.title: Death toll rises to 9 in church attack as officials blame 'extremist' Islamist ideology
articles.excerpt: CCTV in Jordan showed what appeared to be gunmen running toward a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, Jordan, where seven people were killed in what King Abdullah II called an act of terrorism. (Jordan TV...
articles.body_text:
CCTV in Jordan showed what appeared to be gunmen running toward a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, Jordan, where seven people were killed in what King Abdullah II called an act of terrorism. (Jordan TV via AP)

A group of gunmen stormed a Christian church in Jordan during a funeral on Friday, killing nine people and injuring more than two dozen, according to authorities.

The shooting took place at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, about 55 miles south of the capital, Amman.

Jordanian Health Minister Ibrahim al-Budour said Saturday that one critically injured patient remained hospitalized at Prince Ali Military Hospital in unstable condition.

Government spokesperson Mohammad Momani said Saturday that the attackers subscribed to "extremist takfiri ideology," which brands people who reject a strict interpretation of Islam as apostates or nonbelievers. Terrorist groups such as ISIS have invoked takfiri beliefs to justify killing Muslims, Christians and Jews.

Journalists and other people stand outside a Greek Orthodox church cordoned off with crime scene tape hours after gunmen opened fire during a funeral in Hamoud village, in Jordan's Karak governorate on Oct. 23, 2026. (AP Photo)

BISHOP ROBERT BARRON: THE WAR ON CHRISTIANS IS REAL AND THE WORLD CAN NO LONGER STAY SILENT

Karak is home to a sizable Christian minority, and Momani sought to emphasize that Christians are "part of Jordan's national fabric."

It remains unclear whether the gunmen were affiliated with any terror group, and Jordanian authorities have not announced any arrests in connection with the attack.

Footage shown on Jordanian state television showed two gunmen armed with what appeared to be pistols approaching the church and opening fire, The Associated Press reported.

A third man carrying what appeared to be a semiautomatic rifle joined them moments later, before all three rushed toward the church.

People and security forces gather outside a Greek Orthodox Church in the village of Hammoud in Jordan's Karak governorate following a shooting on Oct. 23, 2026. Gunmen killed at least seven people, authorities said. (AFP via Getty Images)

TWO SUSPECTED GUNMEN DEAD, TWO IDF SOLDIERS KILLED IN WEST BANK SHOOTING

Photos and videos from witnesses show broken glass and pools of blood inside the church. After the location was secured by police, two bodies covered with blankets were seen outside the church.

Dorgham Halasa told the AP that intense gunfire erupted in the church some 15 minutes after the funeral service began. People began running, he said.

Halasa said he didn't see the gunmen, but said others he spoke with reported seeing at least four of them. Jordanian authorities had not confirmed the number of attackers as of Saturday.

On Friday, King Abdullah II said Jordan will "confront the terrorist act that targeted Karak with the harshest penalties."

The interior of a Greek Orthodox church is seen hours after gunmen opened fire on Oct. 23, 2026. (AP Photo)

"Whoever imagines that the bullets of treachery can divide the ranks of Jordanians will fail in his endeavor before our steadfastness and unity," he added. "Our deepest condolences to the families of the martyrs, and our wishes for recovery to the wounded."

Jordan announced three days of national mourning following the attack, according to the state-run Petra News Agency.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

James Cirrone is a writer on the Breaking/Trending News team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to james.cirrone@fox.com.

articles.title: Stephen A Smith doubles down on Trump dinner, challenges critics by asking, 'What the f--- are you doing?'
articles.excerpt:
"Straight Shooter" host Stephen A. Smith hit back at critics of his dinner with President Donald Trump on Thursday, asking, "What the f--- are you doing?" as he defended going to the White House.

Ste...
articles.body_text:
"Straight Shooter" host Stephen A. Smith hit back at critics of his dinner with President Donald Trump on Thursday, asking, "What the f--- are you doing?" as he defended going to the White House.

Stephen A. Smith doubled down on defending his meeting with President Donald Trump during an episode of his "Straight Shooter" show on Thursday, challenging his critics by asking, "What the f--- are you doing?"

Smith said during the show he wanted to bring several issues to Trump's attention, but his top priority was to tell the president, "With the squashing of DEI initiatives, it's essentially had a different kind of effect. It's discouraged CEOs of corporations in the private sector to be philanthropic and charitable with their money and give to HBCUs because they're fearful it will be perceived as a DEI initiative being exercised by them."

"I needed the president to speak out against that, and he said he didn't think about that and that is something that he was going to tackle, not to mention the fact he followed up with a call to assure me that's exactly what he was going to tackle in a matter of days when he meets with these HBCU officials. Now I don't know what's going to happen, but I tried, as I always have and as I always will," Smith said.

Smith met with Trump, comedian Bill Maher and musician Kid Rock at the White House on Oct. 15.

JOY BEHAR WANTS TRUMP BACK ON ‘THE VIEW’ DESPITE SAYING HE’S ‘NOT LONG FOR THIS WORLD’

Stephen A. Smith speaks on stage as he and Christopher Russo host SiriusXM shows live from Fanatics Fest at Javits Center on July 17, 2026, in New York City. (Getty Images for SiriusXM)

"All of these folks that are complaining about me showing up to the White House with Bill Maher, what the f--- are you doing? Have you done anything? Are you doing anything? I'm sorry for cussing. I don't mean to, apologizing to the executives at SiriusXM, but damn it. Sometimes we do stuff on the air that we do off the air. This is ridiculous. I mean, it's just, it's never enough," Smith argued.

Smith repeatedly criticized comedian D.L. Hughley during the show, after Hughley questioned Smith's meeting with Trump on the "Uncertain" podcast.

"Why is it that Trump feels so comfortable talking to you when he's shown an aversion to people that challenge him?" Hughley asked during the discussion, as he and his co-hosts criticized Smith for sitting down with the president. "If you challenge him, that's it. Why is it? It isn't that where Stephen A. Smith finds himself his positions, it is that why are people that have a disdain for us so comfortable around you?"

"I think that it says something about you when the people who hate us like you," Hughley added. "Why is it the people that hate my heroes love you?"

Smith criticized Hughley over his comments, saying, "I'm sick and tired of people b----ing and moaning about what needs to be done in our community, but when somebody is actually trying to take steps to do something about it in our own small way, we selling out. We this, we that. What you doing? What you doing? It's a rhetorical question 'cause we know the answer ain't nothing but b----ing."

TRUMP ADMIN'S PUSH TO SCRAP DEI IN FEDERAL GOVERNMENT TAKES LANDMARK STEP WITH NEW HIRING RULE

Smith also defended his Trump meeting during an appearance on "The View" on Wednesday. He told the co-hosts he would not apologize for it.

Co-host Sunny Hostin asked Smith, "He has this history of racial bias that is so clear. Did you think meeting with him, that you got anywhere?"

"I don't know. We'll find out, but he’s the president of the United States, and I’ll be damned if I’m not going to try," he said. "And the reality is I’m just speaking from a constitutional perspective in that regard."

He repeatedly argued that Trump would remain in office until 2028 and that people needed to deal with it.

"You’re going to have to deal with him," he continued. "And when it comes to getting things done, I’m all about exhausting every means and every measure to try to do what’s in the best interest of our community. I’m not apologizing for that to anybody."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Stephen A. Smith speaks on stage as he and Christopher Russo host SiriusXM shows live from Fanatics Fest at Javits Center on July 17, 2026, in New York City. (Getty Images for SiriusXM)

"Stephen A. Smith and Bill Maher, along with John Fetterman, are a dying breed of individuals who believe in the exchange of ideas and positions with those they all may disagree with, as exemplified by the recent dinner at the White House with President Trump and Kid Rock," Fox News contributor Joe Concha told Fox News Digital in a statement about Smith's remarks. "Unfortunately, the trend on the left is to shut down anyone through censorship or otherwise anything resembling debate."

Hanna Panreck is an associate editor at Fox News.

Adolf Hitler's Alpine mountain retreat, known as the Eagle's Nest, was engulfed in flames on Friday night while police arrested a 33-year-old male suspect.

The residence, called the Kehlsteinhaus, is above the town of Berchtesgaden. It was one of several buildings in the area used by the Nazi dictator and his entourage during World War Two.

Hitler also used the area as a backdrop for propaganda films portraying him as a lover of animals and nature.

Local media reported that site had been "largely destroyed", with the public urged to avoid the area.

articles.title: More than 2,000 forced from homes in Hebron amid Israel’s West Bank raids
articles.excerpt: Israel has imposed a lockdown and displaced thousands of Palestinians from their homes in Hebron, as the military conducts raids in the occupied West Bank following the deaths of two Israeli soldiers....
articles.body_text:
Israel has imposed a lockdown and displaced thousands of Palestinians from their homes in Hebron, as the military conducts raids in the occupied West Bank following the deaths of two Israeli soldiers.

This comes as the Palestinian Authority (PA) on Saturday called for international pressure on Israel to protect Hebron’s residents, who said soldiers announced evacuation orders over loudspeakers late at night, leaving them with no time to prepare and few places to move to.

Hebron’s mayor Yousef al-Ja’bari told Al Jazeera that 2,200 people had been forced from their homes as hundreds of Israeli raids took place since Friday’s attack by two Palestinian gunmen on an Israeli army reserve base. The two Palestinians were killed, as well as the two Israeli soldiers.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu then ordered a “full lockdown” of the West Bank following the attack.

Mayor al-Ja’bari said on Saturday that Hebron residents can neither enter nor leave the city.

Israeli soldiers also fired a stun grenade at Al Jazeera journalists near the Farsh al-Hawa checkpoint in Hebron, as they documented an Israeli operation to bulldoze homes and vehicles in the area.

The Israeli military carried out raids across at least 15 areas of the occupied West Bank on Saturday, Al Jazeera correspondents on the ground reported.

Those targeted include Jenin and Nablus in the north; Ramallah, Al-Bireh, Birzeit, and occupied East Jerusalem in the centre; and Bethlehem in the south.

Israeli forces have arrested about 70 Palestinians in raids across the West Bank, the Palestinian Prisoners’ Society said.

The PA, which governs the West Bank, called Israel’s actions “collective punishment”, citing the demolition of homes, forced displacement of entire neighbourhoods, and the “closure and siege of Palestinian cities”, and urged the international community to intervene, Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.

Meanwhile, Hamas said in a statement that the “campaigns and escalations carried out by the occupation and its criminal settlers against our people will only fuel further outrage”.

Around 200,000 Palestinians live in the city of Hebron itself, and a further 600,000 in Hebron governorate, making it the West Bank’s most populous governorate.

Those 800,000 Palestinians in Hebron governorate are “now under siege, with all entrances and exits closed since morning”, Issa Amro, a Palestinian activist and political analyst based in Hebron, told Al Jazeera.

“Inside the city, there is no safe place for anyone to hide … the city is really in fear,” Amro said.

Israeli politicians are trying to “capitalise” on the attack ahead of parliamentary elections on October 27 , Al Jazeera’s West Bank correspondent Nour Odeh said.

“Netanyahu, his Likud party, and his allies in this right-wing coalition are behind in the polls,” said Odeh, so in response they are “trying to put up a brave front, saying they’re combating Palestinians”.

Just days before Israelis are set to vote, Netanyahu avoided answering whether he planned to dismantle the PA, but said a “big surprise” awaits the organisation.

articles.title: Ukraine’s military says Starlink satellite connection stable after recent restrictions
articles.excerpt:
Volodymyr Zelenskyy offers thanks to US allies for restoring system key to air defence and ‘frontline logistics’

Ukraine’s military has a “stable connection to Starlink”, the Ukrainian government has...
articles.body_text:
Volodymyr Zelenskyy offers thanks to US allies for restoring system key to air defence and ‘frontline logistics’

Ukraine’s military has a “stable connection to Starlink”, the Ukrainian government has said, 10 days after its ability to use the satellite communications system was suddenly restricted.

The Starlink satellite terminals, which are produced by Elon Musk’s SpaceX but managed by the US government, are a key component of Ukraine’s military operations. Sudden speed restrictions on the terminals, which capped operations at speeds of 160km/h (99mph), led to the failure of several Ukrainian combat missions earlier this month.

The military’s ability to intercept Russian attack drones was hampered and some Ukrainian operations to strike behind enemy frontlines were cancelled. Russia was able to launch ballistic missiles at Ukraine without any advance warning from the US.

The speed restrictions coincided with the announcement by Donald Trump of a US deal to buy Russian diesel, although the US president initially denied that his administration was behind the decision to cut intelligence sharing with Ukraine.

“I don’t know if it was anybody, but it wasn’t me, and I don’t think it was Elon,” Trump said, referring to Musk, SpaceX’s chief executive.

However, the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, appeared to throw suspicion on Musk when he defended Trump last Wednesday. “The president has nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield and by Mr Musk,” Rubio said. “That’s a private company. The president doesn’t run that company and can’t direct that company to do anything.”

Musk was quick to blame the limits on Starshield on the Trump administration, writing on X last week that the systems were “owned and controlled by the US government”. “Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately Potus [president of the United States],” he wrote.

The US vice-president, JD Vance, backed Musk on Thursday, saying the billionaire “doesn’t want to get in the middle of what is a war between two state actors without the United States government effectively directing him on what to do”.

Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, blamed both parties: “It was a message from [the] American government to limit the speed … And technically, SpaceX did it.”

There were no similar restrictions on Starshield terminals in EU countries and that they applied only to Ukraine, he added. “In other words, this is a planned operation.”

He said the decision would “bring a lot of human losses … of course people would die”.

Announcing the restoration of the system on Saturday in a diplomatic video address on the Telegram app, Zelenskyy expressed his gratitude to his US allies, including Trump and the US state department, for resolving the operational issue: “The most important development for ‌today is that Starlink ‌and Starshield have resumed operations at their pre-restriction speeds. The speeds are now at the ‌level we need.”

The restoration began overnight. “By this morning, the speeds were already sufficient for operational use,” Zelenskyy said. “This is very important and significant for our frontline logistics and for defending Ukraine against jet-powered Shaheds.”

On Thursday, Trump had claimed the service was running again at full speed, but a European official speaking to the Associated Press denied the service was fully functioning.

When asked by reporters whether he would tell Musk to stop “messing around” with Ukraine’s access to Starlink on Friday, the US president said: “I’ve not spoken to him. I might have to … I’ve heard it was fixed. But if it’s not, I’ll speak to him … If there is a problem, I’ll get it straightened out.”

He then described Musk as a “very brilliant” and “very good” person.

Save Women’s Sports activists are surrounded by an agitated group of trans supporters after unfurling a large "Save Women’s Sports" banner and revealing XX-XY shirts at a Portland Thorns match Friday, Oct. 23, 2026. (OutKick)

MOM AND DAUGHTER TOLD TO COVER UP XX-XY T-SHIRTS, SAY THEY WERE THREATENED WITH EJECTION AT FEVER-DREAM GAME

The Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders perform during the game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Baltimore Ravens at AT&T Stadium on Aug. 16, 2025. (Jerome Miron/Imagn Images)

articles.title: Trump's war on drug cartels could gain powerful new ally after pivotal election
articles.excerpt: DEA Administrator Terry Cole joins ‘America Reports’ to discuss expanded U.S. efforts to combat drug cartels in Latin America. Cole weighs in on strategic operations, intelligence sharing, training ef...
articles.body_text:
DEA Administrator Terry Cole joins ‘America Reports’ to discuss expanded U.S. efforts to combat drug cartels in Latin America. Cole weighs in on strategic operations, intelligence sharing, training efforts and maritime security measures aimed at disrupting cartel activity.

EXCLUSIVE: Brazil could join the U.S.-led effort to combat drug cartels if presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro wins the country’s Oct. 25 runoff election, according to his brother, Brazilian politician Eduardo Bolsonaro.

The initiative, known as the Shield of the Americas, is designed to expand security cooperation among countries in the Western Hemisphere, including intelligence sharing, military coordination and joint efforts to disrupt cartel financing.

The coalition follows the Trump administration’s decision in February 2025 to designate eight major criminal organizations as both Foreign Terrorist Organizations and Specially Designated Global Terrorists. The groups include Tren de Aragua, MS-13, the Sinaloa Cartel, the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, the Northeast Cartel, the Gulf Cartel, La Nueva Familia Michoacana and Carteles Unidos.

LATIN AMERICA’S CONSERVATIVE SHIFT FACES ITS BIGGEST TEST YET IN BRAZIL ELECTION

A supporter raises a Brazilian flag next to a U.S. flag during a campaign rally for opposition presidential candidate Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro in São Paulo, Brazil, on Oct. 18, 2026.  (Andre Penner/AP Photo)

"The main thing that we need to do is fight the cartels," Eduardo Bolsonaro told Fox News Digital. "They work together in a lot of countries, so we should fight back then."

Brazil has not joined the initiative under left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Eduardo Bolsonaro said that if his brother’s conservative Liberal Party wins the presidency, Brazil would work with the Trump administration to combat the country’s powerful criminal organizations.

‘DONROE’ DOCTRINE AND CONSERVATIVE VICTORIES SQUEEZE CARTELS IN LATIN AMERICA

"So I’m sure that, under the leadership of President Trump and the Shield of the Americas, we have the opportunity for the first time" to work together against the cartels, Eduardo Bolsonaro said.

Brazil’s presidential runoff will pit Flávio Bolsonaro against Lula after Bolsonaro led Lula in the first round. He has said he would seek closer security cooperation with the United States and other conservative governments in the region.

President Donald Trump, center, Dominican Republic President Luis Abinader, second from left, Argentine President Javier Milei, El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele, Guyana's President Mohamed Irfaan Ali, Costa Rica's President Rodrigo Chaves Robles, Bolivia's President Rodrigo Paz and Chilean President-elect José Antonio Kast pose for a family photo during the Shield of the Americas Summit in Doral, Fla., on March 7, 2026. (Kevin Lamarque/Reuters)

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION CRACKS DOWN ON BRAZIL'S BIGGEST DRUG GANGS WITH ‘GLOBAL TERROR’ DESIGNATION

The potential addition of Brazil would expand the coalition’s presence in South America, where criminal groups such as Primeiro Comando da Capital and Comando Vermelho have become major forces in the regional drug trade.

Other countries participating in the U.S.-led effort include Argentina, El Salvador and Peru. The initiative has also drawn participation from countries including Ecuador, Panama, Paraguay and Chile, according to the State Department.

DRUG CARTEL KINGPIN AMONG TARGETS IN SWEEPING TRUMP CRACKDOWN ON ALLEGED MEXICAN CORRUPTION NETWORK

The coalition’s broader goals include combating drug trafficking, disrupting criminal financing and strengthening cooperation among law enforcement and military officials.

President Trump pictured with former President of Brazil, Jair Bolsonaro. Bolsonaro's son Eduardo spoke with Fox News Digital about a potential new alliance between the two countries. (Evan Vucci/AP Photo; Evaristo Sa/AFP via Getty Images)

U.S. officials have repeatedly linked cartel activity to the trafficking of fentanyl and other illicit drugs into the United States. Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark., has also attributed hundreds of thousands of American deaths to cartel-linked drug overdoses.

articles.title: Storm Boelo to bring 80mph gusts and heavy rain to parts of UK
articles.excerpt:
Second named storm will hit northern parts of UK as thousands remain without power after Friday’s Storm Austen

The UK is bracing for a second storm this weekend, as strong winds and heavy rain are ex...
articles.body_text:
Second named storm will hit northern parts of UK as thousands remain without power after Friday’s Storm Austen

The UK is bracing for a second storm this weekend, as strong winds and heavy rain are expected to disrupt travel and cause further power cuts in the north.

Storm Boelo, the second named storm of the season, is expected to bring heavy, frequent showers and winds potentially exceeding 80mph to northern parts of the UK.

Thousands of homes in the south-west of England have already been left without power after Storm Austen hit the region on Friday.

The Met Office has advised people to stay indoors as much as possible and said the storm will bring danger to life from flying debris and crashing waves.

The forecaster has issued an amber alert, its second most severe weather warning, covering Scotland, the north of England down to Carlisle from 9pm Saturday to the same time on Sunday. Another amber warning is also in place for the north-east of Northern Ireland from 9pm Saturday to 10am Sunday.

A large yellow warning for very wet and windy weather will cover the whole of the UK’s north from midday Saturday to 9pm on Sunday. Another warning for heavy rain covers Wales and parts of western and southern England from 11am to 11pm Saturday.

Widespread travel disruption is expected on ferries and trains. TransPennine Express has warned against making all but essential train journeys on Saturday and Sunday, while Avanti West Coast has strongly advised users not to travel north of Preston on Sunday.

The Met Office has also warned that power cuts across the south-west of England could be replicated across amber areas in the north this weekend.

In the south-west of England, 31,000 homes were without power at one stage on Friday. More than 3,700 were still without electricity on Saturday morning, according to the National Grid map.

Human-driven climate change has continued to reshape rainfall patterns and weather conditions globally. The UK experienced its hottest summer on record this year, with five heatwaves and a record-breaking 40 days of temperatures above 30C.

The Met Office meteorologist Alex Burkill said: “Storm Boelo is arriving. It’s going to bring widespread rain and some very strong winds indeed, and it’s quick on the tails of Storm Austen which is now clearing away towards the east.

“It’s the winds that were perhaps most concerned about, they’re really going to whip up some strong gusty winds across Northern Ireland, northern parts of England and also Scotland through the day – strengthening as we head towards the evening.

“Temperatures will be a little more than the seasonal average but obviously with the wind and rain it’s going to feel pretty unpleasant out there,” Burkhill added. “A very, well, different side of autumn compared with what we’ve seen through much of the season so far.”

Storm Boelo’s winds are expected to peak from Saturday evening. The wet weather will clear overnight in many areas, while more rain continues to hit Scotland and northern Ireland.

Attending a summit on the summer’s record wildfires on Friday, Andy Burnham warned that the UK could face “a winter of greater flooding”.

The prime minister denied suggestions that the government was playing catch-up with civil preparedness, but said “we’re living in a world where unexpected events seem to be becoming more and more common”.

articles.title: College football's NIL and transfer portal chaos on display as nation's top receiver holds absurd ceremony

"I said if your last name was Dakich, you'd be the quarterback at Bowling Green State University, which isn't a bad thing to be. You'd have been on a full ride, but I saw it in high school. I saw the ball come out of your arm. I saw all of it. And I said, he ain't that good."

It's the fourth Saturday of October, folks. Wake up! It's another college football gameday!

The season is just over the halfway point, and the temperature has been cranked way up. We've got conference races coming down to the wire. Playoff hopefuls in must-win situations. Arch Manning might get benched? Half the top 10 teams in the country lost last weekend.

It's just chaos everywhere you look right now, which is why college football is, by far, the best sport in America.

SEC'S CRAZY, HISTORY-MAKING WEEK 7 WEEKEND IS THE LATEST EXAMPLE OF COLLEGE FOOTBALL'S NEW ERA

Jesse Legree No. 12 of the Oregon State Beavers runs after the catch during the first half of a game against the Washington State Cougars at Reser Stadium on Oct. 17, 2026, in Corvallis, Ore. (ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Now, with all that being said, it's also the dumbest sport in America — mainly due to the horrible NIL and transfer portal landscape that we've all created.

And for those who don't believe me, here's Oregon State freshman star Jesse Legree — who is also one of the top receivers in the country — taking time out of his busy week of practice to hold a signing ceremony at his high school to announce ...

... that he's signing BACK with the Beavers for next season.

"What is the major announcement you want to make to the country?" the CBS fellas ask Legree, who is stationed at St. Francis Academy with what sounds like a big crowd on hand.

COUNTRY STAR, FORMER COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYER LEE BRICE RIPS NIL, PRO PLAYERS GOING BACK TO COLLEGE

"I will be signing with the Oregon State Beavers for the 2027-2028 season," Legree, who currently plays for the OREGON STATE BEAVERS, said.

Oregon State Beavers wide receiver Jesse Legree runs for a touchdown against the Colorado State Rams in the first half at Sonny Lubick Field at Canvas Stadium in Fort Collins, Colo., on Oct. 3, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

Look, college football is so broken off the field at this point, I'm not even sure where we go from here. The product on the field is excellent. It's the best show on turf right now, and that includes the NFL.

HERE'S WHY, EVEN WITH ALL ITS PROBLEMS, COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS STILL BETTER THAN THE NFL

But off the field? It's such a joke. This is so absurd, I don't even know where to begin. To channel my inner Mike Gundy:

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Holding a news conference, calling the local TV stations, and announcing to "the country" that you're ... returning to your school next season ... is everything wrong with the current college football landscape. It feels like an SNL parody.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

And by the way, this has nothing to do with Jesse Legree, the player. He's arguably the best wide receiver in the country not named Jeremiah Smith.

The freshman currently leads the nation in receiving yards (1,040), touchdown catches (14) and yards per game (148.6). Not bad! It's only natural that folks would speculate that he's probably hitting the portal next season and going to an LSU, or Notre Dame, or Miami, or Ohio State.

Oregon State's Jesse Legree runs into the end zone for a touchdown during an NCAA football game at Reser Stadium on Saturday, Sept. 12, 2026, in Corvallis, Ore. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

I get it. And honestly, good on Legree for actually returning to Oregon State. You NEVER see kids dance with the partners they came with anymore. They're all one-and-done.

I just don't know that we needed all the theatrics that came with it.

articles.title: Israeli soldiers raze neighbourhood in Hebron, driving families from homes
articles.excerpt:
PM Benjamin Netanyahu vows ‘to destroy this place’ in retaliation for militant attack on army checkpoint

Israeli troops have levelled a neighbourhood in Hebron, driving out hundreds of families in co...
articles.body_text:
PM Benjamin Netanyahu vows ‘to destroy this place’ in retaliation for militant attack on army checkpoint

Israeli troops have levelled a neighbourhood in Hebron, driving out hundreds of families in collective punishment for a militant attack on an army checkpoint outside the West Bank city, local Palestinian authorities said.

The Hebron municipality estimated that 35 hectares (86 acres) had been destroyed or marked for destruction and about 1,500 people had been evicted from their homes by Saturday afternoon in the district of Ein Deir Baha. The whole city of 250,000 people was sealed off by checkpoints on every point of entry.

Videos sent by a Hebron resident showed a substantial area of devastation with every house over several blocks flattened in an urban area. One video showed soldiers marking Palestinian houses with a sprayed black cross, another showed a bulldozer tearing down a stone wall on a hillside and another showed a large residential building festooned with Israeli flags.

People said the building was the home of a prominent Hebron family that had been commandeered as a temporary military headquarters.

The large-scale demolitions follow an attack on Friday on an Israeli military checkpoint outside Hebron by two gunmen. After a 20-minute gunfight, two Israeli soldiers were killed, three injured and the two gunmen were also killed.

Israeli elections will take place in four days and the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, and the extreme-right finance minister, Bezalel Smotrich, travelled to the site of the attack to promise an immediate and ferocious response.

Netanyahu said Israel would “act to destroy this place”. Smotrich who is standing for election in a smaller coalition party, had himself filmed wearing body armour in front of a Palestinian building being demolished. He said he had ordered “the immediate demolition of a wide row of illegal Arab structures adjacent to the attack site”.

Smotrich also called for “a comprehensive military campaign … exactly like in Gaza and Lebanon”. Ein Deir Baha, the focus of the demolitions, was alleged to be the home district of the two gunmen.

A spokesperson for the Hebron municipality said that about 300 families had been evicted. Some had taken refuge in the homes of friends and relatives, while the municipality said it had opened community halls and children’s play areas to shelter others.

A Palestinian news agency, Wafa, reported Israeli plans to displace a further 2,500 people. “We are being collectively punished for something we neither did nor supported,” a Hebron civil rights activist, Issa Amro, said. “Our suffering is being turned into political material for Israel’s elections, while innocent families pay the price.”

Amro said his sister’s family was one of the hundreds driven out of their homes.

“We are talking about hundreds of families who left their homes because of this, and they are not at all connected to what happened yesterday [Friday],” Amro said in a telephone interview. “It’s a very big area and we don’t know what’s going on, whether it is only election propaganda or if it’s a serious plan from decisions on what to do after the election.”

The Israeli army was approached for comment on the operations and on videos showing extensive devastation.

articles.title: FIFA’s Infantino touts global re-election support amid resignation questions
articles.excerpt: FIFA president Gianni Infantino laughed off questions about whether he had considered resigning in the wake of the failed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, pointing to overwhelming support from ...
articles.body_text:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino laughed off questions about whether he had considered resigning in the wake of the failed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, pointing to overwhelming support from member associations around the globe.

Three months after facing calls to resign after he abandoned the proposal that sought private investment in a new entity controlling commercial rights linked to major FIFA competitions, Infantino now finds himself in a position of strength.

His prospects for re-election strengthened on Friday after the head of Asian football endorsed him for a fourth term, with Asian Football Confederation (AFC) President Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa saying Asia was united behind Infantino.

“I was elected by 211 member associations from all over the world. I think what is important is that in an organisation like FIFA, there can be different views, different points of view,” Infantino told the BBC as he laughed off a question about whether he had considered stepping down.

“But if we are serious about democracy, about the democratic process, about believing that everyone has the same vote and the same voice all over the world, that football belongs to everyone … then we need to respect as well the views of the vast, vast majority.

“I’m just coming back off Tokyo where the Asian Football Confederation has fully endorsed me. I was in Cape Verde where all African countries have endorsed me. I’m speaking to all associations everywhere in the world.”

The AFC had previously joined European body UEFA and CONCACAF, which represents North and Central America and the Caribbean, in criticising the FFE proposal.

But a divided CONCACAF and the AFC’s U-turn have left Europe increasingly isolated while exposing the lack of a viable alternative candidate for the FIFA presidency.

Infantino is seeking a fourth term until 2031, and potential candidates must submit their nominations by November 18.

He apologised at a FIFA Council meeting in Zurich last week for the way the FFE proposal was handled, but that did not sway European football associations, such as Germany and England.

However, the 56-year-old Swiss-Italian administrator added: “It’s OK to disagree … but then we need to be able to move on.

“There are different points of view. It’s not always easy to bring them all under one roof, but we need to respect, and I do respect all opinions all views,” Infantino added.

“Then, it will be up to the FIFA member associations to decide who they want as a president and how they want FIFA to be run.”

articles.title: Louvre turns away tourists as Paris braces for renewed violence following destructive riots
articles.excerpt: French President Emmanuel Macron bans illegitimate protests and implements curfews as violent clashes break out across France. Greg Palkot reports live from Paris, where businesses are boarding up win...
articles.body_text:
French President Emmanuel Macron bans illegitimate protests and implements curfews as violent clashes break out across France. Greg Palkot reports live from Paris, where businesses are boarding up windows in anticipation of a fresh wave of protests. The unrest has also forced the cancellation of a Steelers fan event ahead of the NFL international game.

Tourists were turned away from the Louvre on Saturday as some of Paris' most iconic museums remained shuttered amid fears of renewed violence, a week after destructive riots erupted across France.

The Louvre, Musée d'Orsay, Picasso Museum and Grand Palais were all shuttered Saturday as French officials prepared for another weekend of potentially violent demonstrations, according to The Associated Press (AP).

Visitors were seen peering through the Louvre's locked gates Saturday, where a posted notice announced its temporary closure.

TOP TOURIST DESTINATION IN THE WORLD SHUTS DOWN AMID VIOLENT PROTESTS

The museum, home to Leonardo da Vinci's famed "Mona Lisa," was among several major attractions closed amid fears of violent protests.

French officials planned to deploy up to 70,000 law enforcement officers nationwide on Saturday, supported by helicopters, armored vehicles and water cannons, according to the AP.

Visitors arriving at the Louvre Museum in Paris were met with locked gates Saturday as authorities tightened security following widespread unrest across France. (Dimitar Dilkoff/AFP via Getty Images)

The closures came as protesters gathered across France on Saturday, with police rerouting Paris' main demonstration away from the city center to prevent another outbreak of violence.

FURIOUS CROWDS PROTEST SKY-HIGH HOUSING COSTS AND MASS TOURISM IN MAJOR CITY

Shopkeepers were seen boarding up storefronts across Paris, while police stood guard beneath the Arc de Triomphe as authorities braced for another round of unrest.

The Louvre and other major Paris museums remained shuttered Saturday as police rerouted the capital's main demonstration away from the city center to reduce the risk of violence. (Guillaume Saligot/AFP via Getty Images)

The closures also disrupted Art Basel Paris, a major international art fair held at the Grand Palais.

It had opened to the public Friday before organizers canceled the weekend program over security concerns.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The precautions followed a weekend of violent demonstrations that left approximately 3,000 businesses across France damaged or looted, according to the AP.

French authorities prepared helicopters, armored vehicles and water cannons to support a nationwide security operation as demonstrators gathered across the country Saturday. (Nicolas Guyonnet / Hans Lucas / AFP via Getty Images)

The Louvre had already been forced to close earlier in the week after student protesters blocked access to the museum, Fox News Digital previously reported.

Visitors arriving at the Louvre on Monday morning were met with barricades at the museum's iconic glass pyramid, Carrousel du Louvre and Passage Richelieu entrances, as protesters from the École du Louvre blocked access, according to Agence France-Presse (AFP).

The blockade forced museum officials to turn away visitors from the popular attraction, which draws as many as 20,000 people on its busiest days, according to French media reports.

Earlier this week, tourists were left frustrated after being turned away from the Louvre, with one Dutch couple calling the closure "shameful," according to French newspaper Le Monde.

"You are giving Paris a terrible image," the couple said as they held up their tickets.

The U.S. Embassy in France has warned Americans to steer clear of violent protests as widespread unrest prompted curfews and raised concerns about travel disruptions across the country.

The embassy said in a Monday statement that partial curfews had been introduced in several French cities, with additional restrictions possible.

The Louvre, one of the world's most visited and prominent museums, has closed its doors as turmoil sweeps across Paris.  (Anadolu via Getty Images)

Travelers visiting Paris this week were advised to avoid popular protest gathering spots, including Place de la République, Place de la Bastille and Place de la Nation, along with major thoroughfares such as Boulevard Voltaire, which are frequently used for demonstrations, per The Times of London.

Jessica Mekles of Fox News Digital, as well as The Associated Press, contributed reporting.

articles.title: Iran says won’t allow US warships to get close as Trump ponders new attacks
articles.excerpt:
Tehran, Iran – Iran’s armed forces say they are prepared to fire on United States warships as President Donald Trump said Washington was still deliberating new attacks or continued pressure on Iran.

...
articles.body_text:
Tehran, Iran – Iran’s armed forces say they are prepared to fire on United States warships as President Donald Trump said Washington was still deliberating new attacks or continued pressure on Iran.

Trump told supporters at a rally in Florida on Friday that the US military “may do another Epic Fury”, in reference to the extensive bombing campaign against Iran at the start of the war. He had earlier questioned whether to end the conflict quickly through huge attacks on Iran or let pressure on Tehran from a naval blockade and sanctions persist.

But Ali Abdollahi, chief of general staff of the Iranian armed forces, asserted that the US Navy is incapable of re-entering Iran’s territorial waters or its periphery due to Iran’s ability to target any vessel in the region.

“The US president can only dream of their soldiers and military again entering the Persian Gulf. They will take this wish to the grave for good,” he said in a statement carried by state media on Saturday morning.

Abdollahi also said US rhetoric about the war pointed to a basic contradiction: US claims that Iran’s military capabilities have been mostly destroyed during the war were nullified by its refusal to bring its aircraft carriers and support vessels closer to Iranian territory.

He added that Iranian forces were determined to “drown” the US and Israel in a “quagmire” in retaliation for their surprise attack on Iran on February 28, starting an eight-month war and plunging the whole region into instability.

Vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz continue to be attacked by Iran. Together with the increased odds of renewed war, this has driven up oil prices and sent Brent crude to its highest price since April, at about $117.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said seven tankers were attacked or hit mines overnight into Thursday. It then claimed on Friday that two supertankers struck mines. The IRGC has said its military doctrine is now more offensive, and Washington has reportedly ordered many diplomatic personnel to leave Saudi Arabia, with others set to depart other countries in the region.

The Iran-allied Houthis in Yemen also continued to exchange attacks with Saudi Arabia, hitting Riyadh again on Saturday, with the international airport in Dammam and the Shaybah oilfield targeted in recent days. Saudi forces have bombed Marib, Taiz and several other Yemeni provinces under Houthi control.

In southern Lebanon, Friday brought further reported Israeli air attacks around Nabatieh and artillery fire near Zawtar ash-Sharqiyah. Iran has linked this front to its war with the US and Israel, in the past demanding that any ceasefire with Washington also cover Lebanon.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, facing an election on October 27 which comes days before the November 3 mid-term elections in the US, also ordered a lockdown of the occupied West Bank after a Palestinian attack killed two soldiers in Hebron. The Houthis have also launched attacks on Israel linked to events in Gaza and the West Bank, highlighting how wider regional peace now depends on events in multiple theatres, including Lebanon, the occupied West Bank and Gaza.

Netanyahu has reiterated his desire to overthrow the Iranian government, leading several state-linked media and analysts in Iran to claim that Tehran has activated a “dead hand” doctrine. That allegedly enables military attacks against US, Israeli and regional interests to continue from across the country’s 31 provinces if senior Iranian figures are again assassinated as at the start of the war.

The IRGC has threatened seabed internet and communication cables if Iran’s civilian infrastructure is again targeted by the US and Israel. US-based Axios on Saturday cited US intelligence claiming that Iranian authorities had “substantially increased” efforts to strike American officials in the Middle East and beyond.

Mediated negotiations between Iran and the US are no closer to yielding results. But regional and European powers held a coordination meeting in Istanbul on Friday and announced their expectations for the future of the war.

Top diplomats from Turkiye, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt met with the United Kingdom, France, Germany and Italy, with neither the US nor Iran participating.

“We agree that a new attack on Iran would widen the war and spread the conflict across the region,” Turkiye’s Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said after the meeting. “Military intervention in Iran is by no means a solution. No one is endorsing it at this point.”

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said his government held Iran and the Houthis responsible for instability in the Middle East.

But the foreign ministers of the four regional countries issued a joint statement that said “Israeli occupation was the main source of instability in the region and beyond.”

In line with resolving the US-Israel war on Iran, the four regional countries supported the Islamabad memorandum of understanding signed in June and a negotiated settlement, while demanding unrestricted passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The group said they opposed attacks on civilians and commercial vessels, and condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and its Red Sea shipping interests.

The Istanbul meeting once again displayed a “gap between diplomatic claims and realities in the field”, Nour News, an outlet affiliated with Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, argued in an analysis on Saturday.

It said the US and European powers – not Iran – must make concessions first. The outlet presented reopening the Strait of Hormuz as conditional on the US accepting Tehran’s demands and acknowledging responsibility for attacking Iran and Yemen.

Most Iranian newspapers on Saturday focused on signs of war, including rising oil prices.

The headline from hardline Vatan-e Emrooz reported that the price of a barrel of Brent crude rising above $117 was “evidence of disgrace for Trump”. Reformist Etemad said US and Israeli actions were signalling that the “zero hour” of another intense round of the war was approaching.

Reza Nasri, a Tehran-based foreign policy analyst with links to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said that after being subject to decades of attacks, nuclear sabotage, sanctions and violated deals by the US, Iran’s strategy was now “enough is enough.

“Iran has reached its verdict. It will no longer negotiate under bombardment, honour agreements the other side treats as optional, or accept the killing of its children and the penury of its people as routine instruments of policy,” he wrote on X. “It will put an end to this cycle, and it will do so by all necessary means”.

articles.title: Jordan’s King Abdullah orders firm response after deadly church attack
articles.excerpt: Jordan’s King Abdullah has ordered security forces to respond firmly and pursue those behind a church attack in the Karak governorate that killed eight people and wounded 40, the royal court has said....
articles.body_text:
Jordan’s King Abdullah has ordered security forces to respond firmly and pursue those behind a church attack in the Karak governorate that killed eight people and wounded 40, the royal court has said.

The country has already increased security across malls, foreign embassies and other locations across the country in response to the attack, according to the US embassy in Amman, as authorities continue to search for the perpetrators.

On Friday, assailants fired for several minutes in broad daylight during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate, about 120km (75 miles) southwest of the capital, Amman, in what Jordanian authorities described as an “act of extremist terrorism”.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility, as Jordan declared three days of national mourning, according to the kingdom’s Petra News Agency.

King Abdullah, a US partner in the fight against violent armed groups in the region, visited Karak hours after the attack and said the perpetrators would be punished “with an iron fist”.

Prime Minister Jafar Hassan said on X that the attack was “a result of a terrorist ideology and blind extremism”.

“We will not allow society to go down this path,” he added.

Authorities said they were still searching for the attackers, adding that it was too early to determine whether they had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan.

Video footage showed police patrolling outside the church on Saturday.

Nasser al-Burqan, a survivor of the attack, told the Reuters news agency that one of the attackers, standing about two metres (6.5 feet) away, pointed a handgun at him and opened fire on Friday.

A short while later, his son, who also attended the mass, called him to say he had been shot in the leg and was being treated in hospital.

“When everything finally quietened down, I looked out the window behind me, and I saw two [assailants] — one was masked, the other was not; he was carrying a handgun,” said al-Burqan, a lawyer.

“A massacre, a massacre in every sense of the word,” said Tarek Ammarin at a hospital where the wounded were being treated. A relative of Ammarin’s was injured in the attack.

Bahjat al-Rushda, mayor of Shihan village in Karak, joined a list of officials condemning what he called a “wicked” attack.

“God willing, this country will remain safe,” he said.

Such attacks are rare in Jordan, although authorities in the US-allied kingdom say they have repeatedly foiled plots by violent groups motivated by a strict interpretation of Islam in recent years.

Karak is home to a minority Christian population in Jordan, and the country is home to several biblical sites that attract Christian pilgrims from around the world.

On Oct. 19, ABC foreign correspondent Tom Soufi-Burridge said: "The protest Saturday, involving hundreds of thousands of people, were supposed to be about the cost of living, and the state of France’s public services, but the situation quickly spiraled out of control in multiple French cities."

REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: FRANCE BRACES FOR MORE UNREST AFTER PARTS OF PARIS SPUN OUT OF CONTROL

articles.title: Christina Applegate's MS misdiagnosis after 5 years of treatment exposes alarming medical reality
articles.excerpt: Richard Ransohoff, M.D., a Boston-based neurologist who sits on the Board of Directors for the American Brain Foundation, spoke with Fox News Digital about why multiple sclerosis misdiagnoses are comm...
articles.body_text:
Richard Ransohoff, M.D., a Boston-based neurologist who sits on the Board of Directors for the American Brain Foundation, spoke with Fox News Digital about why multiple sclerosis misdiagnoses are common.

Christina Applegate’s recent revelation that she was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis is raising questions about how the disease can be confused with other conditions — even after years of treatment.

The actress, 54, shared the news during an Oct. 20 episode of her podcast, "MeSsy," alongside co-host Jamie-Lynn Sigler, saying she was in a complete "state of shock."

Applegate was first diagnosed with MS in 2021 after experiencing debilitating symptoms and undergoing extensive testing, including brain and spinal MRIs and a spinal tap. She said doctors found dozens of lesions on her brain.

CHRISTINA APPLEGATE SAYS SHE WAS MISDIAGNOSED WITH MS AND IS NOW 'BACK AT SQUARE ONE'

After years of treatment, her doctor decided to stop her regular infusions and monitor her B cells.

"And my B cells didn't change. They didn't go higher, they didn't go lower, they didn't change, and she had never seen that. So I guess that began kind of a study into my diagnosis," Applegate shared.

Christina Applegate’s recent revelation that she was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis is raising questions about how the disease can be confused with other conditions. (AFP via Getty Images)

After additional brain scans, the doctor came into Applegate’s room and said, "Congratulations, you don't have MS."

The actress did not consider this to be good news, however.

"Because you don't get misdiagnosed and then all of a sudden [you’re] better," she said. "I haven't gotten better … If anything, I've gotten worse in some ways."

CARLY SIMON REVEALS THE COMMON CONDITION THAT MASKED HER PARKINSON'S DIAGNOSIS

Applegate noted that she has "every symptom" of someone with MS, adding that there are many conditions that mirror the disease.

"There is no single element in the diagnostic process that tells you with 100% certainty that it is MS."

She recalled that her MRIs clearly showed around 30 lesions, but said her neurologist identified a different feature — which she described as a "string" — that led to the conclusion that she did not have MS.

"So I'm back at square one [and] don't know what's going on with me."

Dr. Marwa Kaisey, an associate professor of neurology at Cedars-Sinai in Los Angeles, said during a follow-up "MeSsy" podcast episode that misdiagnosis of MS is "fairly common."

In a study of patients referred to MS clinics at UCLA and Cedars-Sinai, Kaisey — who has not treated Applegate — said she found that nearly one in five who arrived with an MS diagnosis ultimately did not have the disease.

BRAIN TUMOR FOUND DURING PREVENTIVE SCAN PUTS FULL-BODY MRIS BACK IN THE SPOTLIGHT

"Some [had been diagnosed] for decades," she said. "And a majority of them were on medication to treat their MS."

The primary challenge, according to the doctor, is that there is no single test for MS. "It's not like we have something like a pregnancy test that says, yes, you have it, no, you don't."

Instead, Kaisey said, "It's a list of criteria, some of which remain a little bit subjective."

Most misdiagnosed patients did have some type of white matter spots, or lesions, on their MRI scans, Kaisey noted, but they had a different cause that was not MS.

Newer imaging techniques may help doctors distinguish MS lesions from white matter spots caused by other conditions.

Most misdiagnosed patients did have some type of white matter spots, or lesions, on their MRI scans, Kaisey noted, but they had a different cause that was not MS. (iStock)

Kaisey pointed to the "central vein sign," an MRI finding that looks for small blood vessels running through the center of lesions, which is a characteristic associated with MS. The sign was incorporated into updated MS diagnostic criteria to help doctors determine whether white matter lesions are consistent with the disease.

Richard Ransohoff, MD, a Boston-based neurologist who sits on the Board of Directors for the American Brain Foundation, called the central vein sign "a real step forward" in distinguishing MS lesions from other abnormalities.

"Things are getting better, and even in the time that Ms. Applegate has been having her symptoms and her evaluation, things have gotten better," said Ransohoff, who also has not treated the actress.

SELMA BLAIR'S LAWYER CITES MISSED MEDICATION, HEAD INJURY AFTER IN-FLIGHT ARREST: WHAT DOCTORS SAY

Many of the symptoms of MS — such as tingling or numbness in the feet, fatigue and brain fog — are very common in other conditions as well, according to both neurologists.

"To distinguish MS from its mimics can be challenging, and doctors, even with the best intentions … can sometimes still get it wrong," Kaisey said. "To diagnose MS, we need a symptom that's kind of very specific to MS, and we also need the MRI that looks like MS."

Despite the potential for diagnostic uncertainty, doctors emphasized that the outlook for people who do have MS has improved dramatically. (iStock)

Kaisey said she has found that being "undiagnosed" with MS can be even harder than receiving the initial diagnosis, particularly when the disease has become intertwined with someone's identity, family and community.

"So to suddenly take that away, I think it’s earth-shattering. It's life-changing in a huge way."

EARLY PARKINSON’S SYMPTOMS MISDIAGNOSED FOR YEARS, TERRY CREWS’ WIFE REVEALS

The neurologist emphasized that patients should feel comfortable asking questions and getting a second opinion.

"Don't be afraid to do that, especially if something inside is telling you that you need to dig a little deeper," she advised.

Ransohoff reiterated that MS misdiagnoses are common. "It’s a tough diagnosis, and there is no single element in the diagnostic process that tells you with 100% certainty that it is MS," he told Fox News Digital.

The neurologist said even after a diagnosis, doctors should "keep an open mind" and be willing to reconsider.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"If things start going differently from your expectations, if the person begins to have symptoms that really don't fit in with MS, or they don't respond to treatment, then you really start to put on your thinking cap and say, ‘What else could this be?’"

"It requires the ultimate in humility as a physician. You simply have to say there are certain things we know and certain things we don't know."

Christina Applegate attends the 28th Annual Critics Choice Awards at Fairmont Century Plaza on Jan. 15, 2023, in Los Angeles, California. The actress, 54, shared her misdiagnosis during an Oct. 20 episode of her podcast, "MeSsy." (Getty Images for Critics Choice Association)

Classic early MS symptoms tend to appear relatively quickly, persist for weeks and then recede, according to Ransohoff.

Anything producing a similar pattern can potentially mimic the disease. Some of those conditions may include certain strokes in younger people, neuromyelitis optica spectrum disease (a rare autoimmune disease of the central nervous system), MOG antibody disease (a rare autoimmune inflammatory disorder), lupus and migraine, he said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Migraine is one of the most common alternative diagnoses, both neurologists agreed.

Kaisey noted that migraine can also produce MRI abnormalities in the form of white spots, although they are usually smaller and in a different shape and location.

"Facing the unknown when you feel crappy is a very tough road to go."

"If you're not looking closely at the MRI or you don't know exactly what to look for, you can confuse the two," she said.

In some cases, reversing an MS diagnosis can actually provide a concrete alternative diagnosis and better-targeted treatment — but that did not happen in Applegate’s case, Ransohoff noted.

"You have to have tremendous sympathy for her suffering in that context, because even when treatment is not going as well as you would like, it's better to know what you're dealing with," he said.

"Facing the unknown when you feel crappy is a very tough road to go."

To prevent misdiagnosis, Ransohoff recommends that everyone who receives a multiple sclerosis diagnosis is seen by a specialist at a specialty MS center, who has developed pattern recognition after many occurrences of seeing the disease.

The neurologist noted that MS treatment has advanced dramatically over the course of his career, growing from virtually no options to more than 20 medications today.

Neurologists recommend that everyone who receives a multiple sclerosis diagnosis is seen by a specialist at a specialty MS center. (iStock)

"You want to work with someone who has experience with all those medicines, with all the various patterns that MS can show, because every person's MS is different," he said.

If a treatment isn’t helping or is causing significant side effects, an MS specialist can reassess the approach and help identify a more appropriate medication, Ransohoff added.

The doctor emphasized that the outlook for people who do have MS has improved dramatically.

"The person who's diagnosed with MS today is totally different from 40 years ago when I got started," the neurologist said. "If the diagnosis is correct and the treatment is correct, then they should do pretty well with their MS."

Melissa Rudy is senior health editor and a member of the lifestyle team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to melissa.rudy@fox.com.

articles.title: Missouri businesswoman and single mom killed when police SUV responding to emergency crashes into her Audi
articles.excerpt: Legal expert and criminal defense attorney Donna Rotunno breaks down the investigation into a deadly vehicle crash on a soccer field in Wichita, Kansas. Rotunno also provides analysis on a thwarted Ma...
articles.body_text:
Legal expert and criminal defense attorney Donna Rotunno breaks down the investigation into a deadly vehicle crash on a soccer field in Wichita, Kansas. Rotunno also provides analysis on a thwarted Mall of America terror plot as a Minnesota man faces a federal detention hearing.

A Missouri businesswoman and mother was killed when a police SUV responding to an emergency slammed into her luxury vehicle, raising questions about the deadly crash.

Misty Leslie, 48, died after an Independence Police Department officer driving a 2024 Ford Explorer struck the passenger side of her 2022 Audi SQ5 at an intersection outside Kansas City shortly after 1 a.m. on Oct. 11.

The Independence Police Department said in a statement that the officer was traveling west on U.S. Highway 24 with his emergency lights and siren activated when Leslie's northbound Audi entered the intersection.

REPEAT OFFENDER SLAYS 2 MISSOURI DEPUTIES BEFORE DYING IN SHOOTOUT, SHERIFF SAYS

Police said early evidence suggests the officer had a green light and Leslie had a red light when the crash occurred. Both drivers were wearing seat belts.

Misty Leslie, left, poses with another person in an undated photo. Leslie, a Missouri mother and businesswoman, was killed in a crash involving a police SUV responding to an emergency Oct. 11, 2026. (Credit: ebw_photography_by_misty_ Instagram)

Leslie was taken to a hospital with serious injuries and later died. The officer was also hospitalized but was not seriously injured.

Police have not said how fast either vehicle was traveling or what emergency the officer was responding to. The crash remains under investigation.

The collision comes months after Independence police tightened restrictions on high-speed pursuits following years of scrutiny over the department's driving practices.

DELAWARE STATE TROOPER KILLED IN DMV SHOOTING INCIDENT, GUNMAN ALSO DEAD WITH NO ACTIVE THREAT: OFFICIALS

During a March City Council meeting, interim Police Chief Douglas Brinkley said Independence officers conducted 541 pursuits in 2025, compared with 137 by Kansas City police, The Kansas City Star reported.

Misty Leslie, left, smiles alongside a friend in an undated photo. The Missouri businesswoman and mother died following an Oct. 11 crash involving an Independence police SUV. (Credit: ebw_photography_by_misty_ Instagram)

"I do think we have a reputation for pursuing but we still have to balance that risk versus reward," Brinkley told council members.

A 2024 investigation by the newspaper found that Independence led the Kansas City metropolitan area in high-speed police pursuits. More than 1,200 pursuits across the region in 2022 resulted in over 150 crashes and 51 injuries, with Independence accounting for about one-third of those injuries.

VIDEO SHOWS POLICE OFFICER AMBUSHED IN PATROL CAR IN EXPLOSION OF GUNFIRE, SUSPECT FOUND DEAD AFTER SHOOTOUT

The department revised its policy earlier this year to restrict pursuits for minor traffic violations and city ordinance offenses. Leslie's crash, however, occurred while an officer was responding to an emergency call, not during a reported pursuit.

Fox News Digital has contacted the Independence Police Department seeking details about the officer's speed, the emergency call, his duty status and whether any video captured the crash.

The Independence Police Department headquarters in Missouri. The department is investigating an Oct. 11, 2026, crash involving one of its police SUVs that killed businesswoman and mother Misty Leslie. (Google Maps)

A public records request has also been submitted under Missouri's Sunshine Law seeking crash reports, dispatch records, available footage and the department's emergency-driving policies.

Leslie was a district manager with Signet Jewelers, where she supported the Banter by Piercing Pagoda brand, and owned EBW Photography, a business focused on capturing important moments in people's lives, her obituary said.

Family members remembered her as a determined, competitive leader who cared deeply about her employees and brought passion to everything she did.

But her greatest source of pride was her daughter, Emarea Leslie.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

"Of all the titles Misty held throughout her life, being Emarea's mom was the one that mattered most," the obituary read.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB

Leslie's friend Christel Meinhold also paid tribute to the single mother, describing a close friendship built around raising their children and supporting each other through life's challenges.

Misty Leslie, 48, was a district manager with Signet Jewelers and owned EBW Photography. She was killed in an Oct. 11, 2026, crash involving an Independence Police Department SUV. (Credit: ebw_photography_by_misty_ Instagram)

"If you knew Misty, you knew that woman couldn't do ANYTHING halfway," Meinhold wrote in a Facebook tribute, recalling Leslie's dedication to her career, photography and motherhood.

The women also developed close relationships with each other's children, with Meinhold describing Leslie as an important presence in her son's life.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

"I wish we had one more three-hour conversation that solved absolutely nothing," Meinhold wrote.

A funeral service for Leslie was held Oct. 19 in Lee's Summit, Missouri.

Fox News Digital has also contacted the Missouri State Highway Patrol to determine whether it is assisting with the investigation, along with Signet Jewelers for comment on Leslie's death.

Greg Wehner is a reporter for Fox News Digital covering U.S. news and crime, with a focus on breaking developments, law enforcement, public safety and major stories shaping communities across the country.
